recaps.ending: The grenade-armed trolls attack the goblin sanctuary immediately before the ceremony. Val, Sindari, Willard, Walker, Dimitri, the dwarven mentor, friendly magical guests, and the dragons defend the site. Dimitri's repaired deamplifier weakens troll magic, and Zav kills the final shaman before his suicide attack can harm the gathering. The survivors flee, and no wedding guests are reported killed. Val and Zav then marry in human, goblin, and elven rites. The dragon queen accepts Val as her son's mate and continues productive talks with the rival-clan patriarch, though no peace treaty is confirmed. In the epilogue, the expanded Coffee Dragon reopens. Reb is safe with Inga and begins sword practice with Val and Amber. Nin leaves the magical-weapons trade except for making Val's ammunition, Dimitri continues developing as an enchanter, and Willard and Walker are together. Val and Zav plan a honeymoon, while Val still owes Willard three jobs. Trouble at a lavender farm on the Olympic Peninsula becomes the next assignment. The book closes by returning to the previous Christmas Eve, when Zav brings Amber back from Whistler to join Val's crowded household celebration.
recaps.in_short: Days before Val and Zav's wedding, a grenade damages the Coffee Dragon and a young troll named Reb disappears. Val traces stolen weapons and Reb to hostile trolls who regard her business as a threat, while intensive lessons expand her command of Storm and may explain her worsening exhaustion. Reb is rescued, but the surviving shaman faction attacks the ceremony at the goblin sanctuary. Val's allies, magical-community guests, and the dragons defeat them, and Zav kills the last shaman before his suicide blast can reach the guests. Val and Zav marry after the battle, while dragon peace talks begin without producing a confirmed treaty. The renovated Coffee Dragon reopens, Reb starts training with Val and Amber, and Willard sends Val toward her next unpaid assignment at an Olympic Peninsula lavender farm.

recaps.text: Previously: Val Thorvald, a half-elven investigator, built a life among Seattle's magical community while helping run the Coffee Dragon. She became engaged to the dragon Zavryd and carries Storm, an ancient dwarven sword that she holds only under conditional permission and must eventually return to the dwarven people. Her allies include the magical tiger Sindari, Colonel Willard, enchanter Dimitri, vampire alchemist Zoltan, weapons maker Nin, and her daughter Amber. Val has also met her elven father, the king, and other relatives from his world. Her relationship with that side of her family remains relatively new, while her long absence from Amber's life still makes their bond sensitive. Her coming marriage to Zav will bring together human, elven, goblin, and dragon guests, including Zav's formidable mother. The event therefore carries family and political significance beyond the couple themselves, even before the practical demands of hosting so many different kinds of guests.

So far: Val and Zav's riverside wedding site floods less than a week before the ceremony, and the deposit is lost after Zav eats a cow belonging to the venue. Goblins offer their hidden sanctuary as a replacement. At the same time, an explosion tears apart the Coffee Dragon and injures several patrons. A fragment resembles magical grenade shrapnel, but the attacker remains unknown. Val's elven father arrives with armed relatives, creating tension with Zoltan and crowding Val's home. Zav also brings a dwarven master smith to teach Val how to use Storm. Through exhausting nighttime sessions, Val learns to create a durable barrier and use commands for speed, force, and guided defense. Her increased need for an inhaler concerns her, and a previously defeated elven assassin is seen watching the house, making him a possible but unproven suspect in the bombing.

Val's investigation broadens after Inga reports that her foster son Reb has vanished. Nin identifies the bomb fragment as part of one of her own grenades and discovers that fifteen weapons were stolen from her truck. Sindari finds a faint troll trail, and Willard points Val toward an underground troll bar. Val enters with Sindari and her elven half-sister, whose magic detects the stolen grenades and finds Reb imprisoned in the kitchen. The rescue attempt turns into a fight against armed trolls and a shaman. The attackers remove Reb through another tunnel, leaving behind his toy, food-truck evidence, and a wedding invitation with the date and old venue marked. Val now believes the stolen grenades may be intended for the ceremony, and Reb remains captive.

The elves release Liam after learning that they mistook his intimate encounter with Val's mother for violence. Val's mother then meets the elven king for the first time in decades. The troll threat escalates near Willard's apartment when a shaman arrives carrying the dwarven mentor's monster-summoning box. Val, Sindari, Willard, and Walker defeat the creatures he releases and capture him. Walker reveals a powerful animal battle form during the fight. The prisoner claims that Val and her allies endanger trolls, escapes restraint, and takes Willard hostage. Walker saves her, killing the shaman, and Willard responds to him with an unmistakable sign of affection. The group recovers the box but still has no location for Reb or the remaining explosives. Val and Zav begin searching for the missing mentor while Walker follows Reb's scent.

Val and her companions find the dwarven mentor alive but wounded and infected with troll rot after an ambush. Zoltan develops a treatment, and the recovering dwarf offers to teach Dimitri how to work with a dwarven anvil. Walker locates Reb beneath the monorail. The boy flees onto a moving train, but Val and Sindari prevent him from falling and bring him home safely. Reb admits that he stole a grenade from Val's bag to frighten bullies. Adult trolls then compelled him to serve them, and workers connected to the troll bar bombed the Coffee Dragon under the influence of two shaman brothers. His account places the hostile group in old tunnels beneath Seattle and confirms that its campaign is directed at Val and Dimitri. Reb is safe again, but the group still possesses explosives and remains a threat to the imminent wedding.

The elven assassin approaches Val only to request help acquiring sweets for the Fae Queen, removing him as an immediate threat. Zav's mother arrives and accepts Val as a suitable fighting partner for her son, though she objects to their Earth home. She also brings the prospect of peace talks with a rival dragon-clan patriarch. Dimitri and the dwarven mentor build a portable device intended to suppress magic. Their tunnel search finds that the trolls have left, but a magical message promises revenge before the next full moon. The dwarf suggests that Storm may be draining Val and teaches her a restorative meditation command, which gives her relief before the wedding. At the goblin sanctuary, Val's elven father approves the marriage and agrees to conduct an elven rite. The rival patriarch arrives for talks and openly dislikes Val. As the assembled families and magical community prepare for the ceremony, Walker detects hostile trolls and the first grenades strike the sanctuary.

Val shoots incoming grenades from the air and moves guests to cover while her allies engage the attackers. Dimitri's repaired deamplifier neutralizes hostile magic, and Storm responds to Val's intent with a new fireball ability, though every major use worsens her breathing and fatigue. Friendly trolls, goblins, ogres, orcs, and dragons join the defense. When the last shaman attempts a suicide blast, Zav kills him and magic contains the explosion. The surviving attackers flee, and the dragon queen and rival patriarch pursue them together. With the guests alive, the ceremony proceeds. Val and Zav marry in human, goblin, and elven rites, and the queen personally welcomes Val as Zav's mate. The two dragon leaders continue promising treaty discussions, but no agreement is final. Later, the expanded Coffee Dragon celebrates its reopening. Reb begins sword training with Val and Amber, Nin closes most of her weapons business, and Zoltan turns wedding footage into a large online following for the shop. Val and Zav plan their honeymoon, while Willard calls in one of three jobs Val owes her: investigating trouble at an Olympic Peninsula lavender farm. A closing story returns to the preceding Christmas Eve, when Zav brings Amber home from Whistler so she can join Val's unexpectedly crowded household celebration.

characters.description: The second Hathaway sister, returning from two years of medical treatment in France after scarlet fever left her dangerously weak. Her health and determination have grown, and she intends to build a full life rather than remain the fragile invalid her family remembers. She has loved Kev Merripen since girlhood.
characters.name: Winifred Hathaway

characters.description: A Romani man taken in by the Hathaways as a wounded boy and raised as part of their household. Powerful, taciturn, and fiercely devoted to Win, he oversees the family's estate but believes his violent childhood and intense nature make him unfit to be her husband.
characters.name: Kev Merripen

characters.description: The French-trained physician who supervised Win's recovery at a clinic in France and escorts her home. Cultivated, attentive, and confident in her improved health, he offers the socially acceptable courtship that Merripen refuses to provide.
characters.name: Dr. Julian Harrow

characters.description: Amelia's Romani husband, formerly the manager of a London gaming club. Prosperous, perceptive, and comfortable in both aristocratic and Romani worlds, he treats Merripen as family and notices clues that their unknown pasts may be connected.
characters.name: Cam Rohan

characters.description: Win's protective elder sister and Cam's wife. Accustomed to managing the unconventional Hathaway household, she welcomes Win's restored strength but worries about the pain caused by Merripen's refusal to acknowledge what both he and Win want.
characters.name: Amelia Hathaway

characters.description: The eldest Hathaway sibling and reluctant Viscount Ramsay. Still marked by the death of his fiancée and inclined toward drink and irreverence, he nevertheless sees his sisters clearly and challenges Merripen's habit of turning self-denial into a substitute for honest choice.
characters.name: Leo Hathaway

characters.description: The bookish middle Hathaway sister, nearing the age when the family must consider her London debut. Sensitive and romantic, she observes Win's struggle with sympathy while navigating the affectionate disorder of the household.
characters.name: Poppy Hathaway

characters.description: The youngest Hathaway, an energetic girl with an instinctive affinity for animals and little interest in conventional behavior. Her unusual pets and blunt observations make her a lively presence in the family as Win returns home.
characters.name: Beatrix Hathaway

characters.description: The Hathaways' capable companion and former governess. She brings practical order to the family without trying to make them conventional, and she helps support the sisters as the household prepares for changing social responsibilities.
characters.name: Catherine Marks

recaps.ending: Julian Harrow's respectable courtship gives way to coercion when Win refuses the future he has planned for her. Merripen overcomes both Harrow's threat and his own entrenched belief that keeping away is the only way to protect Win. Win, whose recovery has been a campaign for the right to choose her own life, refuses to accept another man's judgment about what she can endure. She and Merripen finally speak and act on their mutual love, and he commits to marriage rather than retreating again. The investigation into Merripen's childhood also confirms that he and Cam are brothers, giving both men a living connection to the Romani family from which they were separated. The discovery does not erase Merripen's traumatic upbringing, but it disproves his conviction that he is without kin or worthy identity. Surrounded by the Hathaways and newly linked to Cam by blood as well as loyalty, Win and Merripen begin married life with her health restored and his place in the family freely accepted.
recaps.in_short: After two years of treatment in France, Win Hathaway returns to England strong enough to pursue the life she wants with Kev Merripen, the Romani orphan raised with her family. Merripen loves her but rejects her, convinced that his brutal past and consuming temperament would endanger her. Win is courted instead by her physician, Julian Harrow, while Merripen's jealousy exposes the hollowness of his self-denial. Amelia and Cam Rohan support Win, and clues linking Cam's distinctive tattoo to Merripen's lead toward the truth that the two men are brothers separated in childhood. Harrow's polished concern becomes controlling when Win will not submit to his plans. Merripen protects her, but the decisive change is his acceptance that Win can judge her own strength and choose him with full knowledge. Harrow's threat is ended, Merripen claims kinship with Cam and belonging among the Hathaways, and he and Win marry, turning a love long governed by illness and fear into an equal future.

recaps.text: Previously in the Hathaways series: after unexpectedly inheriting a viscountcy and a damaged Hampshire estate, the unconventional Hathaway siblings tried to rebuild their home and enter aristocratic society. Amelia, the eldest sister, married Cam Rohan, a wealthy Romani man who had managed Jenner's gaming club. A past outbreak of scarlet fever killed Leo Hathaway's fiancée, Laura, and left Win physically frail. Kev Merripen, a Romani orphan taken in by the Hathaways as a boy, also survived the illness and has long been silently devoted to Win. Believing England's climate and available care could not restore her, Win left for a French clinic with the family companion, Miss Marks. Cam bears a distinctive tattoo tied to the Romani family he lost in childhood; Merripen carries a matching mark whose significance neither man yet understands.

Win returns to the Hathaway estate after two years in France, visibly stronger and determined to stop living as an invalid. She is accompanied by Dr. Julian Harrow, the physician who directed her treatment and has developed a personal interest in her. Merripen's reaction is intense but divided. He loves Win and is shaken by her transformation, yet insists that his past and temperament would make him a dangerous husband. Win tells him that recovery was meant to create a future with him, not merely to satisfy her family, and refuses to accept evasive tenderness in place of commitment. The household—Amelia and Cam, Leo, Poppy, Beatrix, and Miss Marks—welcomes her while sensing the conflict. Harrow offers admiration, social standing, and open courtship. Merripen throws himself into managing the estate, trying to make self-denial look like protection even as his jealousy makes his feelings unmistakable.

Win tests the freedom her improved health has given her, taking part in family and social life instead of allowing others to decide what will tire or endanger her. Harrow continues courting her and appears to embody a stable future. Merripen repeatedly draws close and then retreats, convinced that the violence of his childhood remains inside him. His possessiveness toward Harrow produces confrontations but not the proposal Win requires. Amelia sympathizes with her sister while Cam and Leo challenge Merripen's claim that rejection is noble. At the same time, Cam notices the likeness between his own mysterious tattoo and Merripen's mark. Questions about the Romani tribe from which both were separated open a path toward Merripen's buried history. He resists that inquiry as firmly as he resists Win, fearing that knowledge will confirm his worst understanding of himself.

Merripen and Win's attraction can no longer be treated as a childhood attachment, but intimacy does not cure his fear. Win makes clear that she will not surrender her chance for marriage and children while he decides indefinitely on her behalf. Harrow presses his advantage and moves toward a formal claim on her, encouraging Merripen to believe a gentleman and physician can give her the safe life he cannot. Yet Harrow's solicitude increasingly treats Win's health as a reason she should obey him. The search into Cam and Merripen's origins advances through their matching marks and surviving Romani knowledge. Evidence suggests that their connection is not coincidence and that Merripen was separated from close kin before the abuse that shaped his childhood. For Cam, the possibility offers family; for Merripen, it threatens the isolated identity around which he has built his defenses.

Win refuses to choose Harrow merely because Merripen continues to reject her. As Harrow realizes that medical authority and conventional status will not secure her consent, the controlling quality beneath his courtship becomes clear. Merripen is forced to see that withdrawal has not kept Win safe; it has left room for another man to disregard her wishes while claiming to act for her benefit. The Hathaways rally around Win, and Cam continues following the evidence of his shared past with Merripen. Their investigation indicates that the two men are brothers who were separated when young. The discovery gives context to Merripen's scars and matching tattoo without making his later suffering inevitable or shameful. He begins to understand that the family he serves is not his only accidental refuge and that his capacity for fierce attachment need not be expressed only through sacrifice and silence.

Harrow attempts to impose his will after Win rejects the future he has designed for her, and Merripen intervenes to end the threat. The crisis strips away his last argument for distance: Win is not the frail girl he remembers, and she chooses him with a clear understanding of both his love and his damage. Merripen finally stops using her former illness and his childhood as reasons to control the decision. He declares his love and commits himself to her openly. The clues from the men's past confirm that Cam and Merripen are brothers, giving Merripen a blood relationship alongside the place he has long held within the Hathaway household. Cam welcomes the bond, while Merripen begins accepting that survival did not make him unworthy of family. Win and Merripen marry with the support of the Hathaways. Her hard-won health becomes the beginning of an independent adult life, and his devotion changes from watchful renunciation into a partnership she has freely chosen.

characters.description: A nine-year-old Vietnamese American girl who lives beside a rubbish-filled vacant lot in Cleveland. Hoping to feel connected to the father she never knew, she secretly plants lima beans there in the cold soil. Her small private act becomes the beginning of the community garden.
characters.name: Kim

characters.description: An elderly Romanian immigrant who has watched the neighborhood from her apartment for many years. Suspicious when she sees Kim burying something in the vacant lot, she investigates and accidentally harms one of the seedlings before realizing that the girl has planted beans.
characters.name: Ana

characters.description: A school janitor whose life has been shaped by other people's demands. Ana asks him to help save Kim's damaged bean plants, and caring for them gives him a task he has chosen for himself. His childhood on a Kentucky farm gives him practical knowledge of growing things.
characters.name: Wendell

characters.description: A Guatemalan boy who has learned English more quickly than the older members of his family and often serves as their interpreter. In the garden, he discovers that language is not the only kind of expertise when his great-uncle immediately understands the soil and plants.
characters.name: Gonzalo

characters.description: Gonzalo's elderly great-uncle, a former farmer from Guatemala who is isolated in Cleveland because he speaks no English. The vacant lot restores his confidence: he reads the ground, improvises tools, and begins cultivating a plot without needing translation.
characters.name: Juan

characters.description: A determined woman who wants to grow goldenrod in memory of her grandmother. Confronted by the lot's heaps of refuse, she carries a bag of its most revolting rubbish through city offices until officials can no longer ignore the neighborhood's problem.
characters.name: Leona

characters.description: A retired man who enjoys bringing strangers together. He sees the emerging garden as a chance to make the neighborhood more humane, hires help for his own plot, and notices that the gardeners' fences and groupings reproduce some of the divisions found outside the lot.
characters.name: Sam

characters.description: A Haitian boy whose father takes over the plot Sam has paid someone to cultivate. The family plants baby lettuce as a business venture, placing adult hopes and financial pressure on a crop that is vulnerable to heat and other setbacks.
characters.name: Virgil

characters.description: A Korean immigrant who withdrew from other people after a violent robbery at her dry-cleaning shop. The sight of neighbors working in the garden draws her out again, and she joins them by planting hot peppers and contributing funnels so that water can reach the dry soil more effectively.
characters.name: Sae Young

characters.description: A physically imposing young man who plants tomatoes as part of his effort to win back Lateesha, a woman he once neglected. He guards the plants closely and employs Royce to watch them, but his private display gradually draws him into the garden's wider community.
characters.name: Curtis

characters.description: A homeless teenager who initially sleeps in the garden. Curtis hires him to protect a valuable tomato crop, and the work gives Royce a recognized place among the gardeners, who begin feeding him and treating him as part of their community.
characters.name: Royce

characters.description: A British nurse who cares for Mr. Myles, an elderly man who communicates only through gestures. When he signals that he wants to visit the garden, she helps him establish a flower bed and finds herself becoming an eager gardener as well.
characters.name: Nora

characters.description: Nora's elderly client, who uses a wheelchair and can no longer speak. He makes his wish to join the garden clear by pointing, then selects flowers by responding to their pictures, asserting preferences that his physical condition often keeps hidden.
characters.name: Mr. Myles

characters.description: A pregnant Mexican American teenager who is resentfully attending a program for expectant mothers. At first she has little interest in the group's garden plot or in her pregnancy, but watching the plants endure and change begins to alter how she imagines the life ahead of her.
characters.name: Maricela

characters.description: An Indian immigrant who runs a fabric shop and grows eggplants in the lot. The garden lets him meet neighbors who had previously been only distant faces or stereotypes to one another, though he also witnesses how quickly fear can revive old divisions.
characters.name: Amir

characters.description: A woman who considers herself a watcher rather than a gardener. Remembering ancestors who planted their first crops after reaching freedom, she observes the lot through its first year and recognizes its growers as a new group of seedfolks putting down roots.
characters.name: Florence

recaps.ending: By the end of the growing season, the garden has changed both the vacant lot and the relationships around it. People who once knew one another only as members of unfamiliar ethnic or social groups have exchanged food, advice, labor, and protection. Royce has gained a place in the community, Sae Young has recovered some trust in strangers, and Maricela has begun to see new life with less despair. The cold eventually empties the plots and leaves Florence worried that the community may vanish as quickly as the plants. In early spring, however, she sees Kim return to the lot and kneel in the same place to plant lima beans again. The act that began the garden is repeated, showing that the shared project will continue into another year.
recaps.in_short: In a Cleveland neighborhood divided by language, age, ethnicity, and poverty, nine-year-old Kim plants lima beans in a rubbish-filled vacant lot to honor the father she never knew. Ana notices the child, Wendell tends the seedlings, and one resident after another begins cultivating the ground. Their accounts show the lot being cleared and transformed into a community garden. Gonzalo sees his isolated great-uncle recover his authority as a farmer; Leona forces the city to remove the rubbish; Sae Young regains trust after a traumatic robbery; Curtis uses tomatoes to reach out to a former girlfriend; and other growers find livelihood, purpose, or companionship. The garden does not erase conflict, and fences sometimes reproduce the neighborhood's divisions, but shared work and harvests create connections that did not exist before. After winter arrives, Florence sees Kim return to plant lima beans again, beginning the garden's second cycle.

recaps.text: Kim, a nine-year-old Vietnamese American girl, slips into a rubbish-filled vacant lot beside her Cleveland apartment building and plants lima beans. She wants to honor the father who died before she was born and imagines that tending a crop will let his spirit recognize her as his daughter. Ana, an elderly Romanian neighbor, watches from her window and suspects that Kim has hidden something illicit. When she digs up the spot to investigate, she discovers the beans and realizes she has damaged one. Troubled by what she has done, she asks Wendell, a janitor with farming experience, for help restoring the seedlings.

Wendell revives Kim's beans and, tired of spending his life responding to other people's problems, clears a patch where he can plant something of his own. The lot begins to offer its neighbors new roles. Gonzalo, a Guatemalan boy accustomed to translating for his family, follows his wandering great-uncle Juan there. In the city Juan has seemed helpless because he speaks no English, but among soil and seedlings the former farmer immediately becomes capable and purposeful. Gonzalo recognizes that the balance between them has reversed: the old man understands this world without an interpreter. With more than one person now cultivating the ground, Kim's secret memorial is becoming a shared garden.

Leona decides to plant goldenrod in memory of her grandmother but first confronts the mountains of refuse covering the lot. After telephone calls bring no action, she carries a leaking bag of the worst rubbish into a public office and waits until officials respond; the city finally clears the site. Sam, a retired man who makes a habit of talking to strangers, sees the garden as a small paradise where the neighborhood might meet. He arranges for a teenager to prepare a plot and plant pumpkins for him. Yet he also notices that gardeners cluster by background and put up fences, bringing the surrounding community's separations into the new space even as they work beside one another.

Virgil's father tries to turn the garden into income by crowding a plot with baby lettuce, but heat and practical difficulties threaten his plans. Sae Young, a Korean shopkeeper left fearful and isolated after a violent robbery, is drawn to the sight of people working together. She plants hot peppers and supplies funnels that make watering easier, gradually recovering a sense of safety among neighbors. Curtis plants tomatoes where Lateesha, the woman he hopes to win back, will see them. Protective of the crop, he pays a homeless teenager named Royce to guard it. The gardeners begin bringing Royce food and including him in their work, giving him an accepted place in the community rather than treating him as an intruder.

Nora, a British nurse, brings her nonverbal client Mr. Myles to the garden after he signals his interest. She helps him choose and plant flowers, and the activity reveals preferences and enthusiasm that his disabilities had concealed from others. Maricela arrives with a program for pregnant teenagers, angry about her pregnancy and indifferent to the assigned plot. As the season turns, she observes that plants can look finished and still carry the beginnings of future growth. The garden does not solve her situation, but it helps her imagine change and approach the child she is carrying with less rejection. The lot has now become a place where vulnerable people can exercise choice and see themselves differently.

Amir, an Indian fabric-shop owner who grows eggplants, reflects that the garden has introduced people who previously passed one another as strangers. He sees neighbors share produce and knowledge, although a tense misunderstanding also shows that suspicion has not disappeared. Florence, who calls herself a watcher rather than a gardener, compares the growers to ancestors who established themselves by planting in new ground. The harvest and cold weather eventually empty the lot, and she fears the fragile community will not return. Then, in early spring, Florence sees Kim come back to the original patch and plant lima beans once more. The girl's private memorial begins another growing season, confirming that the garden and the connections formed around it have survived the winter.
